trust_decision.summary: The social-login callback trusts redirect_to decoded from the client-returned, unsigned base64-JSON OAuth `state` and uses it as the post-login redirect Location; the sanitized value set at login page time is not bound to the state (fix: keep redirect_to server-side in cache keyed by an opaque single-use state).

landing_point.why: Summary says 'unsanitized OAuth state param'; grepping state/redirect leads straight to login_oauth_user reading state['redirect_to'] and passing it to redirect_post_login.

fix_sites.entry_point: same callbacks as above, redirect branch (generate_login_token falsy)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All fix hunks are in frappe/utils/oauth.py; the login page producer (frappe/www/login.py:93) is unchanged. Out-of-scope-looking sibling is an O8 route (google_oauth.callback), not a published fix site.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: frappe/integrations/google_oauth.py:callback is the Google *integrations* (Contacts/Indexing/Mail authorisation) callback, not social login, requires a logged-in user, and the advisory names only the social-login state; a solver can argue it is a different feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate post-login redirect to the sanitized same-host redirect-to captured on /login (absolute same-host URL or path) must still work after social login, and the default desk/website redirect when none is given; for the Google integrations callback, relative /desk/Form/... redirects with success/failure query params must keep working. Also login_oauth_user's public signature accepts a dict state and existing tests pass {'token': ...}.

O6_input_shapes: state as base64-encoded JSON string (decoded at frappe/utils/oauth.py:209-211)
state as an already-decoded dict (frappe/utils/oauth.py:202, used by tests at frappe/integrations/doctype/social_login_key/test_social_login_key.py:38)

O7_producer.where: frappe/utils/oauth.py:99-108 serialises redirect_to into the round-tripped state (base64 JSON); value originates from frappe/www/login.py:29-30,93

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Google integrations OAuth callback takes `redirect` from client-returned plain-JSON state and sets it as the Location with no sanitisation or server-side binding (reachable with error= and no code).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Different feature (Google Contacts/Indexing/Mail authorisation, not social login), whitelisted for logged-in users only, and the advisory only names the login flow.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file and package (frappe/integrations vs frappe/utils); state producer in frappe/integrations/google_oauth.py:103-119, callers in frappe/integrations/doctype/google_contacts/google_contacts.py:64 and frappe/website/doctype/website_settings/google_indexing.py:25

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Connected App flow currently stores success_uri server-side in Token Cache and checks state equality (frappe/integrations/doctype/connected_app/connected_app.py:217,232); a variant that round-trips success_uri inside state would be a realistic second implementation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same 'carry the return URL through OAuth state' idiom already used by google_oauth.py and pre-fix utils/oauth.py.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: login_via_token could realistically accept a redirect_to argument passed straight to redirect_post_login (mobile/app login-token handoff).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: login_oauth_user's generate_login_token branch (frappe/utils/oauth.py:244-248) hands off to login_via_token, which drops the redirect; a maintainer restoring it would forward a client value.

O9_family: open_redirect (CWE-601) via unauthenticated client-round-tripped OAuth state

O10_build.toolchain: Python 3.10+/bench, Node/yarn for assets (not needed for these tests)
O10_build.project_tests: frappe/integrations/doctype/social_login_key/test_social_login_key.py (mocks OAuth2Service.get_auth_session, calls login_via_oauth2 with dict state)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Call frappe.www.login.sanitize_redirect on state['redirect_to'] inside login_oauth_user (string-path only), leaving the state unbound and google_oauth.callback untouched.
